__comment__: Per-instance value overrides for seed.py, keyed by graph name then instance index.
These pin the literals the Cypress specs pick dropdown options by; everything else
on the resource keeps seed.py's generated filler.
Why the split at instance 4: coral's generate_ha_name_function builds the display
name as '{smr_number} {site_name}' as soon as ANY reference number is present, and
only as '{ha_number} {site_name}' when none is. 02_flag_for_enforcement searches for
'HA/02', so instances 1-3 must carry no reference numbers at all - hence the nulls
on smr/ihr/hb/historic_parks. 09_state_care's launcher runs an advanced search for a
non-null SMR Number, so instances 4-6 carry one.
Six instances, not five: arches sets minimumResultsForSearch: 5, below which selectWoo
renders no search box at all (see cy.select2Search in cypress/support/commands.js).

display_name is deliberately NOT seeded: generate_ha_name_function creates that tile itself on the first save (Tile.get_blank_tile_from_nodegroup_id), so supplying one too gives two tiles for a cardinality-1 nodegroup and the import fails.

monument_name is the CONSTANT 'Testing', not 'Testing {n}'. 02_flag_for_enforcement asserts the exact text of the associated resource: cy.contains('Associated Resources:').siblings().should('have.text', 'HA/02 Testing'). A per-instance suffix would render 'HA/02 Testing 2' and fail that equality. This also matches how the display names look in a real coral database.

Instances 7-9 are named 'Garden Test', not 'Testing', and exist ONLY for 01_add_garden's three 'open an existing HA' tests. Those tests drive an existing Heritage Asset through the Add Garden workflow, and merely opening it rewrites its display name - if the test then fails part way through, the asset is left with a BLANK name. When they shared the 'Testing' assets they silently wiped the names off HA/01-03, and 02_flag_for_enforcement (which runs later in the same CI run) then found an unnamed option instead of 'HA/02 Testing'. Keeping them on their own assets, matched by a search term the other specs do not use, restores isolation. Note the whole suite runs against ONE database in CI, so anything a spec mutates is visible to every spec after it.
